title: Autonomic revert prober with synthetic-load simulation and state harmonizer
creator: Anya Patel
description: Problem: configuration changes (batching, cache policies, kernel selection) sometimes cause subtle degradations that only show under specific request patterns; automatic rollbacks can be noisy or too aggressive and may not restore runtime state (KV cache, batch windows). Goal: build an autonomic 'revert prober' that validates a config apply by running targeted synthetic load simulations, snapshots runtime state, and can safely stage an automatic revert with state reconciliation if degradation is detected. The prober should operate as a lightweight pre- and post-apply validator, a post-failure investigator, and a controlled auto-revert executor with guardrails to prevent cascade rollbacks and data divergence.
acceptance_criteria: Prober runs pre-apply simulations with representative synthetic traces and produces a compatibility score (0-100) within the console UI
On post-apply, prober executes a short synthetic workload and compares latency/cost/kv-consistency against baseline; downgrades score triggers staged revert candidate
Automatic revert only executes after quorum of signals: cost-surge, latency-90th regression > configured SLO delta, and KV cache divergence metric above threshold
State reconciliation routine captures and restores necessary in-memory metadata (KV cache quarantine metadata and batch-window pointers) or marks safely for warm-start to avoid double-processing
All actions are logged in audit trail with snapshot references; can be manually promoted or fully reverted by on-call within 15 minutes
End-to-end test harness covering synthetic pre/post scenarios and a failure-mode where revert is executed; test passes on CI with golden baselines
design_notes: Use commitless staging: apply config to a canary slice with mirrored traffic and synthetic probes before global rollout
Synthetic traces derived from sample of 3 production tenants representing low/medium/high token-length distributions
KV cache divergence detection via deterministic prefix checksums sampled across replicas (cheap sampled telemetry), not full snapshot
Backoff strategy: soft-fail (traffic-shift + throttle) then hard-revert only when metric quorum persists for X minutes
Make prober idempotent and side-effect-free: synthetic probes use read-only paths and sandboxed model instances where possible
implementation_plan: 1) Schema: extend config-change event with preapply_snapshot_id and postapply_snapshot_id
2) Telemetry: add small-sample prefix checksumming and latency-cost microbench markers
3) Simulation runner: containerized synthetic driver that can target canary nodes, with workload templates stored in S3
4) Orchestrator: state machine that transitions through PREAPPLY -> APPLY -> POSTCHECK -> QUORUM_EVAL -> REVERT/CONFIRM
5) Reconciliation: KV quarantine API and warm-start hooks to selectively invalidate or rebuild cache entries
6) UI: console panel showing compatibility score, probe output, and one-click approve/revert
7) Safety: require 2-step approval for cross-tenant global reverts and rate-limit auto-reverts to N per day per environment
telemetry_and_alerting: Audit log entry for every automated revert: includes snapshot ids, probe traces, and decision rationale
Dashboard: correlation panel for cost-per-token, batch size distribution, and kv-divergence by model variant
rollout_plan: Alpha: run prober in passive mode on staging and a small canary set (internal tenants) for 2 weeks
Beta: allow automated suggestions (no auto-revert) for 1 month, capture operator feedback
GA: enable auto-revert with conservative thresholds and 2-hour cooldown windows; expose controls in Dedicated and Private admin panels
Migration: provide opt-out flag on existing rollout policies and a migration job to attach preapply baselines
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives cause unnecessary reverts -> Mitigation: require quorum of orthogonal signals and progressive backoff
Risk: state reconciliation may leave caches cold causing transient cost spikes -> Mitigation: implement warm-start hints and staggered rebuilds
Risk: attacker could trigger synthetic probes -> Mitigation: probes run with internal credentials, rate-limited and tagged in audit logs
Risk: heavyweight probes increase noise in telemetry -> Mitigation: use sampled, short-duration workloads and isolate probe telemetry
comments: 2026-02-21 Anya Patel: Initial writeup and scope. Decided to prioritize KV divergence detection and synthetic preapply checks. Asked infra for a test cluster.
2026-02-26 Marcus Li: Spike completed for prefix checksum sampling. Initial numbers show sub-1% cost overhead for 1k samples per minute. Adding flag to toggle sampling frequency.
2026-03-02 Design review (Sofia Ramirez): UI wireframes look good; requested clearer explanation of compatibility_score algorithm and a help tooltip for operators.
2026-03-05 Security review (Liam O'Connor): Approved with note to ensure probe credentials are short lived and recorded in audit logs. Added requirement to rotate probe keys monthly.

2026-03-10 Marcus Li: Implemented orchestrator state machine and staged canary runs. Two minor issues: snapshot retention policy and race when postapply probe starts before cache warmup. Filed ENG-64899 to follow up.
2026-03-12 Anya Patel: Demo scheduled for 2026-03-15 with SRE and Product. Next steps: tune thresholds and add 2-step approval for multi-tenant rollbacks.
